Documentation

# BuildonOwl.

Everything your team needs to deploy Owl on your claims systems: concepts, API reference, integrations, and the security model behind it.

01Documentation

## Startwhereyouare.

Eight categories, from the first connection to the model cards behind every output. Pick the one that matches the question in front of you.

01

### Getting started

Provision your single-tenant VPC, connect your first claims system, and read your first file with Owl in under a day.

[View→](https://owl.co/documentation#)

02

### Core concepts

How Owl models the file, and why every output carries a span-grounded citation back to the page it came from.

[View→](https://owl.co/documentation#)

03

### API reference

Endpoints, request and response schemas, authentication, rate limits, and webhooks for every Owl product.

[View→](https://owl.co/documentation#)

04

### Integrations

First-party connectors for Guidewire, FINEOS, Origami, DXC, and Majesco, plus a generic ingestion path for the rest.

[View→](https://owl.co/documentation#)

05

### Security & compliance

The data-handling, tenancy, and audit model: SOC 2, single-tenant processing, and the controls behind every release.

[View→](https://owl.co/documentation#)

06

### Data taxonomy

The shared vocabulary Owl uses for claim entities, document types, and evidence, so your team and ours speak the same language.

[View→](https://owl.co/documentation#)

07

### Model cards

What Owl-1.5 and Owl-Bench are trained on, evaluated against, and validated for, with their published limitations.

[View→](https://owl.co/documentation#)

08

### Changelog

Every release, model update, and breaking change, dated and versioned, so you always know what shipped and when.

[View→](https://owl.co/documentation#)
